title: Criminal Complaint: State of Wisconsin v. Tehrangi N. Chapman

reports.title: Second member of the Milwaukee Police Department charged with misuse of license plate reader system
Criminal Complaint: State of Wisconsin v. Tehrangi N. Chapman

summary:
Milwaukee Police Detective Tehrangi Chapman was charged with felony misconduct in public office and misuse of a GPS device. A complaint says he admitted using the Flock license plate reader system 20 times to track two people, including 17 searches for one person's vehicle from January 2024 to January 2025 and three searches for another person in January 2025. He also admitted installing a GPS device on one vehicle. Chapman, a 22-year internal affairs veteran, has been suspended since March 13 and is due in court July 17. His attorney was unavailable.

The charges follow Officer Josue Ayala, who pleaded guilty to attempted misconduct in June and resigned after being accused of using the system to check vehicles tied to someone he dated and that person's ex. Milwaukee officials called the new charges troubling, and the police chief said no one is above the law. The department has changed system access and audits. Some Wisconsin communities, including Verona, Dane County, UW-Madison and Kaukauna, have ended or declined to renew Flock contracts.
